proof:
# Exact noheavy root frontier and a conditional near-BM three-fiber theorem

This is a conditional theorem about a critical cap or critical cap cover
with controlled captured-root deficit. It does not prove that such a
cap or cover exists for arbitrary convex fibers. The whole-volume
optimization below is exact among its stated numerical constraints.

## 1. Sharp noheavy whole-volume bound

Let d>=1 and let A,K,B be positive d-dimensional convex bodies with
(A+B)/2 subset K. Write a=|A|^(1/d), c=|K|^(1/d), b=|B|^(1/d)
and M=|A|+|K|+|B|. Suppose no fiber exceeds M/2. Define B_d as the
unique number in (1,2) satisfying

    B_d^d-(2-B_d)^d=1,

and put y_d=(2-B_d)^d. Then

    M <= [1+B_d^d+(2-B_d)^d]|K|
       =2(1+y_d)|K|
       <(1+sqrt(5))|K|.                             (1)

Existence and uniqueness of B_d follow from strict increase of
x^d-(2-x)^d on [1,2], where its values bracket 1. Normalize c=1
and exchange endpoints if necessary so b>=a. BM gives a+b<=2.
If b<=1, a^d+b^d<=2, which is no larger than B_d^d+(2-B_d)^d
by convexity of the power. If b>=1, the noheavy condition gives
b^d<=1+a^d<=1+(2-b)^d, hence b<=B_d. Since
x^d+(2-x)^d is nondecreasing for x>=1,

    a^d+b^d <= (2-b)^d+b^d
               <=(2-B_d)^d+B_d^d.

This proves the nonstrict bound. It is attained among whole bodies
by homothetic fibers with roots 2-B_d,1,B_d; their midpoint is exact
and the large endpoint has exactly half the total volume.

For the strict dimension-independent estimate, put x_d=B_d^d.
Then x_d-y_d=1 and

    x_d y_d=[B_d(2-B_d)]^d<1,

because B_d is strictly between 1 and 2. Hence
y_d(1+y_d)<1, so

    y_d<(sqrt(5)-1)/2.

Substituting in 2(1+y_d) proves the last part of (1). This argument
also covers d=1, where B_1=3/2 and the exact first bound is M<=3|K|.

## 2. Exact combination with endpoint volume floors

Still normalize c=1. Suppose additionally a^d,b^d>=h, with 0<=h<=1.
Set

    L=max(2-B_d,h^(1/d)).

Then the exact maximum of M under BM, noheavy, and these two floors is

    M <= 1+L^d+(2-L)^d.                             (2)

Indeed L<=1. If b<=1 the sum of endpoint volumes is at most 2,
which is no larger than L^d+(2-L)^d. If b>=1, the preceding argument
gives b<=B_d, while a>=h^(1/d) and a+b<=2 give
b<=2-h^(1/d). Thus b<=2-L, and monotonicity of
x^d+(2-x)^d on [1,2] proves (2).

Conversely the roots a=L,c=1,b=2-L satisfy every numerical
constraint: b<=B_d gives its noheavy condition, the middle is
nonheavy because a^d+b^d>=2, and both endpoints meet their floors.
So the scalar bound is exact. This does not assert that any additional
prescribed critical-cap data can be realized at this maximizing triple.

## 3. Apply the frontier to one actual critical cap

Let S be exactly the three fibers at -1,0,1, with mixed d-volume M.
Let a closed ambient halfspace with nonzero continuous normal attain
raw depth Q at the actual point (0,y), y in K. Write its three
captured volumes U,q,V. Suppose

    q>=Gamma_d |K|,
    U^(1/d)+V^(1/d)>=2(1-eta)q^(1/d),  0<=eta<=1,

where Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d. Put

    p=q/|K|, T=(U+V)/q, A_eta=2(1-eta)^d.

Convexity of the power gives T>=A_eta. Keeping this cap's continuous
normal fixed, a sufficiently large finite integer tilt captures the
entire first endpoint and none of the other, and the opposite tilt
reverses their roles; both preserve middle capture q. Criticality
therefore gives

    |A|,|B|>=U+V=Tp|K|.                              (3)

BM then implies Tp<=1. Under noheavy, apply (2) with h=Tp and restore
the scale |K|. Since Q=(1+T)p|K|,

    Q/M >= (1+T)p/
          [1+L(Tp)^d+(2-L(Tp))^d],

    L(h)=max(2-B_d,h^(1/d)).

The denominator is nonincreasing in h on [0,1], because
x^d+(2-x)^d is nonincreasing for 0<=x<=1. Increasing p or T thus
increases the numerator and cannot increase the denominator.
Using p>=Gamma_d and T>=A_eta yields the explicit frontier

    Q/M >= (1+A_eta)Gamma_d /
            [1+L_eta^d+(2-L_eta)^d],                 (4)

    L_eta=max(2-B_d,(A_eta Gamma_d)^(1/d)).

The argument covers d=1, for which the denominator's power sum is
constant, and every endpoint cut status. No differentiability or
positive captured endpoint volume is assumed. The products in (4)
are feasible: A_eta Gamma_d<=2Gamma_d<=1.

## 4. Exact and uniform sufficient deficit thresholds

Even without the finite-tilt refinement, (1) gives

    Q/M >= (1+T)Gamma_d/[2(1+y_d)].                  (5)

Consequently T>=y_d suffices for Q/M>=Gamma_d/2. A sufficient
captured-root deficit condition is the exact dimension-dependent
threshold

    eta<=1-(2-B_d)/2^(1/d).                         (6)

The dimension-independent comparison y_d<(sqrt(5)-1)/2 gives the
simpler sufficient threshold

    eta<=1-[(sqrt(5)-1)/4]^(1/d),

under which Q/M>Gamma_d/2 is strict.

A convenient rationally stated condition is

    eta<=1/(d+1).

It gives T>=2(d/(d+1))^d=2Gamma_d>2/3. Here Gamma_d>1/3 follows
from (1+1/d)^d<e<3; both exponential comparisons follow directly
from the binomial and exponential series. Also sqrt(5)<9/4, since
5<81/16. Equations (1) and Q=(1+T)q now give the explicit strict
margin

    Q/M > [(5/3)/(13/4)]Gamma_d
          =(20/39)Gamma_d>Gamma_d/2.                (7)

This rational margin is deliberately weaker than the exact frontier
(4), but holds uniformly in every d>=1.

## 5. Heavy fibers and a conditional cap-cover corollary

If a fiber D has volume at least M/2, choose its ordinary centroid
g_D at that fiber's integer base. For any closed ambient halfspace
containing that point, its restriction to D either contains the
whole fiber or is a continuous halfspace containing g_D. Ordinary
Grunbaum gives at least Gamma_d |D|>=Gamma_d M/2 in either case.
Thus a heavy fiber supplies the desired OC point independently of
any middle-source cap structure.

For a conditional theorem covering both alternatives, assume a point
(0,y) admits finitely many depth-attaining ambient caps with nonzero
continuous normals whose middle traces cover K, and each cap has
captured-root deficit at most eta q^(1/d) in the displayed sense.
If a heavy fiber exists, use its centroid as just described. Otherwise,
some middle trace contains the ordinary centroid of K and therefore
has q>=Gamma_d |K|. Apply (4)--(6) to that cap. Under (6), one of
these specified deterministic choices has every containing halfspace
of mass at least Gamma_d M/2. Under eta<=1/(d+1), the noheavy choice
(0,y) has the stronger margin (7); the heavy-fiber case is only
claimed to satisfy the OC constant.

This is not a proof for arbitrary three-fiber bodies: the existence
of the depth-attaining middle cap cover with the stated small root
deficits is an explicit hypothesis. The theorem does not establish
such a deficit bound, nor treat arbitrary numbers of integer fibers.

## Measure and center scope

All three whole fibers are positive d-dimensional convex bodies, so
their finite union has intrinsic Hausdorff dimension d and measure M.
All selected points belong to their actual fibers. Criticality controls
every closed ambient halfspace through the definition of raw depth.
The saturated tilt comparisons are finite and use strict capture or
exclusion at endpoints. Ordinary centroid arguments do not discard
vertical boundary-fiber mass. No lattice-coordinate normalization,
approximation, limiting point, or unproved geometric stability result
is invoked.
